status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: Strong cross-cutting candidate: support for building more housing ('pro-supply') appears on both left and right, as does neighborhood protection.

items.stem: Should cities allow more homes to be built in neighborhoods now zoned only for single-family houses?
items.scope: Think about neighborhoods in cities and suburbs with high housing costs.
options: Yes, require cities to allow apartment buildings in most neighborhoods
Yes, allow duplexes and townhomes, but not large apartment buildings
Let each neighborhood decide
No; keep single-family zoning

definitions.text: Zoning is local law that sets what can be built where, such as only one house per lot.

items.stem: Should state governments override local zoning to get more housing built?
items.scope: State laws that require cities to allow more homes than local rules do.
options: Yes, whenever cities fall short of housing goals
Only near public transit and job centers
No; zoning should stay local

items.stem: Should new housing that already follows the zoning rules be approved without public hearings or lawsuits that can delay it?
items.scope: Projects that meet every building and zoning rule.
options: Yes, approve it automatically
Yes, after a short public comment period
No; neighbors should have a say through hearings and the right to sue

items.stem: Should cities be allowed to limit how much landlords raise rent each year?
items.scope: Limits for existing tenants in existing buildings.
options: Yes, strict limits, such as no more than inflation
Moderate limits, such as inflation plus a few percent, with new buildings exempt
Only temporary limits during emergencies
No limits

items.stem: Should landlords need a specific reason, such as unpaid rent, to evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease?
options: Yes, for all tenants
Only for tenants who have lived there a year or more
No; landlords can end a lease when its term ends

items.stem: Should every low-income family that qualifies for federal rent help receive it?
items.scope: Rent vouchers that pay part of a family's rent to a private landlord.
items.context: Today only about 1 in 4 eligible households gets federal rental help, because funding is limited.
options: Yes, every eligible family
Help more families than today
Keep about today's level
Help fewer families; rely more on the private market

facts.claim: Only about 1 in 4 households eligible for federal rental assistance receives it
facts.source: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities analysis of HUD data

items.stem: Should government build and own more housing itself?
items.scope: Housing owned and managed by a government agency.
options: Yes, a large amount, for people of all incomes
Yes, for low-income people
No; pay private builders through tax credits to build affordable housing instead
No; leave housing to the market

items.stem: What should cities do about people camping on sidewalks and in parks?
items.scope: Think of people with nowhere else to sleep that night.
items.context: In 2024 the Supreme Court ruled that cities may ban public camping even when shelters are full.
options: Allow it until enough shelter or housing is available
Clear camps only after offering each person a shelter bed
Ban camping and clear camps, even without enough shelter beds
Ban camping, with fines or jail for people who don't move

facts.claim: City of Grants Pass v. Johnson (2024): enforcing public camping bans is not cruel and unusual punishment

items.stem: For homeless people with addiction or mental illness, which approach comes closest to your view?
options: Housing first, with no requirement to be sober or in treatment
Housing first, but treatment is required to keep it
Treatment or sobriety first, before getting housing

items.stem: Should it be easier to require treatment for people living on the street with severe mental illness who refuse help?
items.scope: Today this is usually allowed only when someone is an immediate danger to themselves or others.
options: No; keep treatment voluntary except for immediate danger
Somewhat easier: also when they can't meet basic needs like food and shelter
Much easier, including longer required hospital stays

items.stem: Should large investment firms be allowed to buy single-family homes to rent out?
items.scope: Firms owning hundreds or thousands of homes.
options: No, ban it
Allow it, but with limits or extra taxes
Yes, they add rental housing

items.stem: Should cities limit short-term rentals like Airbnb in residential neighborhoods?
items.scope: Whole homes rented to visitors by the night.
options: Ban them in most neighborhoods
Allow them only in the owner's own home
Allow them with registration and taxes
No limits

items.stem: Should homeowners be able to deduct mortgage interest from their federal income taxes?
items.scope: Today this deduction mostly benefits higher-income homeowners who itemize.
options: No; end it and use the money for renters or first-time buyers
Keep it, but only for smaller mortgages
Keep it as is
Expand it to help more homeowners

items.stem: How should transportation money be split between public transit and roads?
options: Much more to transit, less to new roads
Somewhat more to transit
Keep about today's split
More to roads and highways
